Shape: backcountry
Leaving from: Québec City
Going to: Parc national de la Gaspésie
Dates: 3 nights somewhere between 2027-08-15 and 2027-09-15
Travellers: 2

Access needs: not answered
Budget: shoestring, as a feeling rather than a figure
Appetite for effort: demanding

Experience: some

candidates.title: Mont Albert summit loop via La Table du Pique-nique
candidates.summary: Classic demanding alpine day on the Chic-Chocs plateau with arctic-alpine tundra and caribou habitat. Cloud navigation is a real risk on the plateau; only go in clear forecast, and stay on the marked route. Access needs were not answered, so terrain suitability is not accounted for. Distance and time depend on the route chosen.

candidatesAccepted.title: Québec City to Parc de la Gaspésie by car, first half
candidatesAccepted.summary: Drive the St. Lawrence south shore on Route 132 as far as Rimouski, which is about 3 hours of driving and is a sensible overnight-free break point before the park. Fuel and parking are the main costs; I could not account for access needs, which were not answered, so check rest stops yourselves. This is a movement option only and not clearance to go anywhere.

candidatesAccepted.title: Rimouski to Parc de la Gaspésie by car, second half
candidatesAccepted.summary: Continue along Route 132 to Sainte-Anne-des-Monts and then up Route 299 to the park's discovery centre area. Together with the first half this keeps each driving leg short enough for a long day. Access needs were not answered, so I could not account for them.
